title: Black Benny, Louis Cottrell and press rolls
summary: Martyn asks how Benny and Cottrell played; Watkins says Benny never read, Cottrell did, and all used press rolls.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Can I stop you for a minute?
Yeah. Well, say with the earlier drummers, you know, like Black Benny and Louis Cartrell, see? Did they play more of the same stuff as you're playing today, sort of?

No. Well, yeah, Black Benny did. Yeah. But you see, Louis Cartrell, he did more reading. Yeah. He got his, he done his most of the reading, not from, not from, from the ear. Yeah. And Black Benny, well, he never did read. No. Yeah. But he take a lesson here in the morning like I did. That's where he learned his beats. Yeah.
But they use more or less the same press roll beats then?

Oh yeah, same press rolls. Yeah, they use most of the, more, use that more or less. Yeah. Which you take all jazz drummers, always use a press roll. Yeah. But you'd rather sell them if you notice any big bands or any small combos. You never catch the drummers using press rolls.
